_doc: Icons (v0.8.4.43), read only by IconRules.of. An icon is a file assets/icons/<kind>/<id>.png; `shared` gives one file to several ids, `source` says where a file came from. With no file: an item takes its plain base's icon (ItemRules.plain_of) with the marks below, else its group's; a spell is the blank of its kind in its school's colour with marks of its damage and shape; anything else the blank of its kind, then _blank/default.png. Marks and colours are drawn by the interface, no picture is needed for them; a file assets/icons/marks/<what>/<id>.png replaces a mark's dot.

portraits._doc: v0.8.4.43.5.2, read only by PortraitRules.of: a face for a token, a portrait and a card. A person of a race of the game is people/<race>/<male|female>/<age>__<n>.webp (race — an id of races.json, age — a key of rules.body.age), anybody else its template's monsters/<template>__<n>.webp; n from 1 to the `variants` of its age (`by_age` overrides), chosen by the id, so a person keeps one face. A record's own `look.portrait` comes first. No file — the letter. Drawn by tools/anima, 256 px, a square with the face in the middle (the ring cuts a circle).

shared._doc: "<kind>/<id>": "<kind>/<id>" — the second's file stands for the first. «slots/<slot>» — the faded picture of an empty slot of the doll (v0.8.4.43.6); «toggles/<id>» — a passive of rules.toggles on the hotbar (v0.8.4.43.7).

source._doc: "<kind>/<id>": where its file came from — forge (tools/anima), hand, or a licence line (CC BY …).

ui._doc: Icons of the interface itself: window buttons, needs, acts of a place. The id is the file ui/<id>.png, the value its subject for the artist.
ui.sheet: the character: a bust of a hooded adventurer
ui.deeds: a bundle of tools: hammer, quill and coin
ui.weapon_set: two crossed swords with an arrow
ui.place: a hand over a table with things
ui.board: a notice board with pinned papers
ui.sneak_wait: a crouching figure with an hourglass
ui.exit: an open door with an arrow
ui.wilds: a bow and a fishing rod
ui.faith: a temple altar with a flame
ui.nonlethal: a club wrapped in cloth with stars over it
ui.details: an upright sheet with lines of text

rarity._doc: The frame of an item by its rarity; none for a common thing.

schools._doc: A spell's school colour by `school_id`: the tint of its icon with no file of its own and the frame of its button in the sheet (v0.7.22.21, the eight schools muted to the «dark book»).

elements._doc: A mark of a damage type: on an item by its property <type>_damage, on a spell by `damage_type`.

materials._doc: A mark of a material: by an item's property, its `material` or the start of its id (adamantine_…).

shapes._doc: A mark of a spell's area by `area.type`.

buttons._doc: A button of the interface by its node name → its icon ui/<id>, or a whole ref «<kind>/<id>» (a gathering spot by its thing, v0.8.4.43.14); a key ending with «*» takes every name that begins so.

frames._doc: v0.8.4.43.23, read only by UiTheme.skin and UiTheme.frame: the interface's frames in the lines style (the author's pick of 2026-11-12), drawn by tools/anima/ui/paint.py and cut by tools/anima/ui/frames.py into <root><file>.png. A part's `cut` is the margin of its nine pieces in the drawn picture's px and `scale` the drawn px to the game's (the corners keep their size, the edges and the middle stretch); `files` are the pictures made of a part, `look` how its picture is changed (hover, pressed, disabled, warm — the main button's gold, on and off — a tab); `slots` give a style of the project's theme («Type/style») a file, laid as a StyleBoxTexture with the content margins of the flat style it replaces, wider by the part's `pad` [across, down] — how far its drawn line stands inside the edge, so the text keeps the gap it had from the flat border (the author, 2026-11-12: «текст начинается слишком от края»). The ornaments are laid by code where the theme has no place for them: the divider's mark in the middle of every HSeparator (UiTheme.adorn), the ring round a portrait with its HP in the ring's channel (Portrait). `look` of an ornament: lit — its brightness as alpha, line and mark — a divider's stretched line and its middle mark; a file's own `scale` stands over its part's (the mark larger than the thin line). A file not drawn leaves the flat style: the art is not kept in git.
